key_insight: Free-stream forcing in hypersonic blunt-body boundary layers is first amplified near the nose by a slow-down convection effect, then further boosted downstream by lift-up, producing large non-modal transient growth.
engineering_relevance: The asymptotic model helps predict receptivity and disturbance amplification in hypersonic vehicle boundary layers, informing thermal protection and stability design.
method: High-Reynolds-number asymptotic analysis of the receptivity process
Identification of a nose-region slow-down convection mechanism
Reduced-order model for downstream evolution of non-modal perturbations
evidence_signal: The reduced model is reported to agree well with SF-HLNS calculations across the receptivity and downstream growth stages.
watch_item: The asymptotic theory is tailored to high-Reynolds-number blunt-body flows, so accuracy may degrade away from the assumed regime or when wall-temperature/nose-radius effects are outside the calibrated range.
paper_title: Excitation of non-modal perturbations in hypersonic boundary layers by free stream forcing. Part II: asymptotic theory and key mechanisms
